title: 7 Days in Japan
subtitle: Kyoto, Nara and the Kansai hills
bestTime: Late March to mid-April, or November
travelTime: Two internal transfers; everything else on foot or by local train
overview: A first Japan trip that resists the Tokyo–Kyoto–Osaka sprint. Seven days in Kansai, based almost entirely in Kyoto, with day trips out to Nara and the cedar hills. The argument is simple: one base, deep coverage, no packing and unpacking.
packing: Comfortable walking shoes you can slip off easily — you will remove them several times a day
A small folding bag for temple visits
Layers; Kyoto is colder in winter and more humid in summer than most visitors expect
A cash card that works at Japanese ATMs, plus some cash
An IC transit card, loaded on arrival

dayPlan.morning: Land at Kansai and take the Haruka express into Kyoto station.
dayPlan.afternoon: Check in, then walk the Kamo river path to shake off the flight.
dayPlan.evening: An early izakaya dinner in Pontocho and an early night.
dayPlan.transport: Kansai airport to Kyoto, 75 minutes by train

dayPlan.morning: Philosopher's Path at 7am, then Nanzen-ji before the crowds.
dayPlan.afternoon: Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama lanes.
dayPlan.evening: Kaiseki dinner, booked well in advance.

dayPlan.morning: Nishijin weaving district with a working weaver.
dayPlan.afternoon: Nishiki market, then the Kyoto craft centre.
dayPlan.evening: Obanzai counter dinner in Nakagyo.

dayPlan.morning: Move west; bamboo grove at 6.30am if you have shifted hotels.
dayPlan.afternoon: Tenryu-ji gardens and the Hozu riverbank.
dayPlan.evening: Ryokan kaiseki and a private onsen.
dayPlan.transport: 25 minutes by train from central Kyoto

dayPlan.morning: Train north to Kurama and walk the cedar ridge to Kibune.
dayPlan.afternoon: Onsen at Kurama on the way back.
dayPlan.evening: Return to the ryokan; dinner in-room.
dayPlan.transport: Eizan line, roughly 30 minutes each way

dayPlan.morning: Early train to Nara; Todai-ji before the coaches.
dayPlan.afternoon: Kasuga Taisha's lantern paths and the deer park.
dayPlan.evening: Back to Kyoto for a final dinner in Gion.

dayPlan.morning: Fushimi Inari at first light, then the sake district below it.
dayPlan.afternoon: Luggage forwarding, then the Haruka to Kansai.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.

title: 10 Days in Italy
subtitle: Naples, the Amalfi Coast and the islands
bestTime: May, early June or late September
travelTime: One train, the rest by ferry and bus
overview: Ten days built around the Amalfi coastline, travelled the way it works best — by ferry, from a single base, with two nights in Naples at the start for the food and the archaeology. No hire car, deliberately.
packing: Shoes with grip: this coast is built entirely from steps
A light layer for evening ferry crossings
Swimwear you can walk to the beach in
A dry bag for boat days
Modest cover-up for church visits

dayPlan.morning: Arrive, drop bags, walk the Spaccanapoli.
dayPlan.afternoon: The Archaeological Museum, which holds everything removed from Pompeii.
dayPlan.evening: Pizza in the historic centre, then a walk along the seafront.
dayPlan.transport: Naples airport to the centre, 20 minutes

dayPlan.morning: Train or transfer to Sorrento, then ferry along the coast.
dayPlan.afternoon: Check in; swim at Marina di Praia.
dayPlan.evening: Dinner on the terrace as the coast lights come on.
dayPlan.transport: Ferry from Sorrento, roughly an hour

dayPlan.morning: Bus up to Bomerano and walk the ridge path westward.
dayPlan.afternoon: The long stair descent into Positano; swim, then ferry back.
dayPlan.evening: Early dinner — this is a tiring day.

dayPlan.morning: Ferry to Amalfi; the duomo and the paper museum.
dayPlan.afternoon: Walk fifteen minutes to Atrani, which is where people actually live.
dayPlan.evening: Return by ferry in the late light.

dayPlan.morning: A slow morning; swim before the day boats arrive.
dayPlan.afternoon: Lunch on a working lemon terrace with the family that farms it.
dayPlan.evening: Nothing scheduled.

dayPlan.morning: Move up to the ridge, 350m above the coast.
dayPlan.afternoon: Villa Cimbrone's belvedere, then Villa Rufolo.
dayPlan.evening: A concert if the festival is running; otherwise the gardens at dusk.

dayPlan.morning: Private or shared boat around the island rather than the day-tripper route.
dayPlan.afternoon: Anacapri and the chairlift, avoiding the Marina Grande crush.
dayPlan.evening: Back to Ravello for the last dinner.
dayPlan.transport: Boat from Amalfi, roughly an hour

dayPlan.morning: Transfer down to Salerno or Naples.
dayPlan.afternoon: Flight or onward train.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.

title: 14 Days in Thailand
subtitle: Bangkok, the northern hills and the Andaman coast
travelTime: Two internal flights, one overnight train
overview: The classic Thailand shape done properly: a short city start, a full week in the north where the culture and the landscape are, and a coastal finish that is a rest rather than a second trip.
packing: Light layers — the north is genuinely cool in December and January
Modest clothing for temples: shoulders and knees covered
Reef-safe sunscreen for the coast
A dry bag
Insect repellent for the hills

dayPlan.morning: Wat Pho and the river ferries; skip the tuk-tuk touts entirely.
dayPlan.afternoon: Chinatown food walking, then a rooftop for the scale of the city.
dayPlan.evening: Overnight sleeper train north, or fly.
dayPlan.transport: Sleeper train to Chiang Mai, 12 hours

dayPlan.morning: Doi Suthep before sunrise, then the old city temples.
dayPlan.afternoon: Northern Thai cooking class; the cuisine is not Bangkok's.
dayPlan.evening: Food trail through the old city and Chang Phueak.

dayPlan.morning: Full day at an ethical sanctuary — no riding, no bathing.
dayPlan.afternoon: Continue north into the Mae Rim hills.
dayPlan.evening: Check in above the coffee valleys.

dayPlan.place: Mae Rim and the Samoeng loop
dayPlan.morning: Drive or ride the Samoeng loop through the coffee hills.
dayPlan.afternoon: Spa afternoon, or the Mae Sa waterfall walk.
dayPlan.evening: Dinner at the lodge; early night before the flight.
dayPlan.transport: Hire car or driver for the loop

dayPlan.morning: Fly south to Krabi or Phuket, then transfer to the coast.
dayPlan.afternoon: Four days of islands, longtail boats and doing very little.
dayPlan.evening: Sunset on the beach; the trip's decompression.

dayPlan.morning: Transfer to the airport.
dayPlan.afternoon: Fly home or connect via Bangkok.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.

title: Solo Vietnam Journey
subtitle: Central Vietnam at a walking pace
travelTime: One internal flight, one coastal train
overview: Nine days for a first solo trip to Vietnam, built around central Vietnam rather than the full north-to-south run. Small towns, short transfers, one place you stay long enough to have a regular coffee spot.
packing: A bicycle-friendly daypack
Rain layer, even in the dry season
A padlock for guesthouse lockers
Small denomination cash for markets
A power bank for long transfer days

dayPlan.morning: Arrive via Da Nang or Hue; the citadel in the morning cool.
dayPlan.afternoon: The royal tombs by boat along the Perfume river.
dayPlan.evening: Hue's food is distinct from anywhere else in Vietnam — eat widely.
dayPlan.transport: Fly into Da Nang or Hue

dayPlan.place: Hai Van Pass to Hoi An
dayPlan.morning: The coastal train or a car over the Hai Van Pass.
dayPlan.afternoon: Check in across the river from the old town; collect a bicycle.
dayPlan.evening: First walk through the lanterns.

dayPlan.morning: Old town walking early, before the tour groups.
dayPlan.afternoon: A tailor consultation, if you want one — commission one considered piece.
dayPlan.evening: River-side dinner and the night market.

dayPlan.morning: Market-to-table class starting at the central market.
dayPlan.afternoon: Rest through the heat; swim.
dayPlan.evening: Quiet dinner; you will not be hungry.

dayPlan.morning: Cycle out through Tra Que to the fishing village.
dayPlan.afternoon: Move to the beach for the last stretch.
dayPlan.evening: Sunset from the sand.

dayPlan.morning: Swim, read, cycle in for lunch in the old town.
dayPlan.afternoon: Cham Islands boat trip if the sea is calm.
dayPlan.evening: Beach restaurants; the local crowd arrives around six.

dayPlan.morning: Transfer to Da Nang.
dayPlan.afternoon: Fly out or continue south.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.

title: Luxury Rajasthan Escape
subtitle: Udaipur, the Aravallis and the desert forts
travelTime: Private car throughout; one internal flight
overview: Eight days across southern Rajasthan at a pace that suits the heat and the architecture. Two bases rather than five, a private car, and the fort-and-temple days scheduled around the light rather than around a tour operator's clock.
packing: Light cottons and linens; evenings in December are genuinely cold
Modest cover for temples
Sunglasses and a hat — the light is intense
A scarf, useful for temples, dust and air conditioning
Comfortable shoes for fort stairs

dayPlan.morning: City Palace at opening, before the courtyards fill.
dayPlan.afternoon: Old city craft lanes and miniature painting studios.
dayPlan.evening: Lake Pichola boat in the last hour of light, then a rooftop dinner.
dayPlan.transport: Fly into Udaipur; on foot in the old city

dayPlan.morning: The Ranakpur Jain temple — 1,444 carved pillars, no two alike.
dayPlan.afternoon: Kumbhalgarh's fort walls, the second-longest continuous wall in the world.
dayPlan.evening: Return to Udaipur, or overnight in the Aravallis.
dayPlan.transport: Private car, roughly 3 hours each way

dayPlan.morning: Move out to rural Rajasthan; village walks at first light.
dayPlan.afternoon: Leopard tracking in the Jawai hills, or simply the pool.
dayPlan.evening: Dinner under the stars.

dayPlan.morning: Back to Udaipur; block printing or miniature painting session.
dayPlan.afternoon: Bagore ki Haveli and the ghats in the afternoon light.
dayPlan.evening: Final rooftop dinner facing the palace.

dayPlan.morning: Slow morning by the lake.
dayPlan.afternoon: Fly out via Delhi or Mumbai.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.

title: Himalayan Road Trip
subtitle: Shimla to Spiti to Manali, the slow way
travelTime: Long driving days on mountain roads; this is the trip
overview: Twelve days across the Spiti circuit, entered from Shimla so that altitude is gained gradually and exited over Kunzum to Manali. The route is the itinerary — the driving days are not transfers between the good bits, they are the good bits.
packing: Layers for a 25°C daytime and 0°C night swing
Diamox if your doctor advises it, plus a plan for altitude symptoms
Cash — ATMs are unreliable above Reckong Peo
A BSNL SIM, the only network with real coverage
Sun protection: UV at 4,000m is severe

dayPlan.morning: Drive up through the Kinnaur valley along the Sutlej.
dayPlan.afternoon: Sangla and the Baspa valley, around 2,700m.
dayPlan.evening: First night at moderate altitude — this is deliberate.

dayPlan.morning: Kinnaur Kailash from Kalpa at sunrise.
dayPlan.afternoon: Cross into the cold desert; the landscape changes completely at Nako.
dayPlan.evening: Nako lake, 3,600m; sleep low if you feel unwell.

dayPlan.morning: Tabo monastery, founded in 996, with its original murals.
dayPlan.afternoon: Dhankar's cliff monastery and the walk to Dhankar lake.
dayPlan.evening: Continue to Kaza, the valley's main town.

dayPlan.morning: Key monastery for morning prayers.
dayPlan.afternoon: Rest and acclimatise properly before going higher.
dayPlan.evening: Kaza has the valley's only real services — restock here.

dayPlan.morning: Up to the high villages at 4,400m; fossil fields above Langza.
dayPlan.afternoon: Hikkim's post office, among the highest in the world.
dayPlan.evening: Village homestay, eating with the family.

dayPlan.morning: Over the Kunzum pass at 4,550m, road conditions permitting.
dayPlan.afternoon: Chandratal lake; camp only at the designated site.
dayPlan.evening: The coldest night of the trip.

dayPlan.morning: The descent through Batal and Gramphu — the roughest stretch of the route.
dayPlan.afternoon: Arrive in Manali; the drop in altitude is immediately noticeable.
dayPlan.evening: A proper hot shower and a proper meal.

title: 45 Days Across South India
subtitle: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and the coast
travelTime: Trains and hired cars; no internal flights required
overview: A long, deliberate journey through the four southern states, moving roughly every four to five days rather than daily. This is the itinerary for a sabbatical, a long leave or a first slow-travel experiment — the pace is the product.
packing: Light cotton throughout; one warm layer for the hill stations
A good daypack and a lockable main bag
Water purification — you will be refilling constantly
Modest clothing for temples across all four states
A rail booking account set up before you travel

dayPlan.morning: Fort Kochi's colonial quarter and the Chinese fishing nets.
dayPlan.afternoon: Mattancherry, the spice warehouses and the synagogue.
dayPlan.evening: Kathakali performance, then a slow start to the trip.

dayPlan.morning: Estate walks at first light with plantation staff.
dayPlan.afternoon: Eravikulam, Top Station, and the Kolukkumalai jeep track.
dayPlan.evening: Verandah evenings on a working estate.

dayPlan.morning: Spice plantations around Kumily.
dayPlan.afternoon: Down to Alleppey; a night on a houseboat, then a homestay.
dayPlan.evening: Backwater villages by canoe rather than by houseboat.

dayPlan.morning: Marari or Varkala; the trip's first genuine rest.
dayPlan.afternoon: Ayurvedic treatment courses run properly over several days.
dayPlan.evening: Beach and nothing else.

dayPlan.morning: Madurai's Meenakshi temple at the 5am opening.
dayPlan.afternoon: Thanjavur and the Chola bronzes; Chettinad's mansions and cooking.
dayPlan.evening: Long train legs between towns — book sleeper class ahead.

dayPlan.morning: The French quarter early, before the heat.
dayPlan.afternoon: Mahabalipuram's shore temples and stone carving workshops.
dayPlan.evening: Coastal seafood and a slower rhythm again.
dayPlan.transport: Train and road along the coast

dayPlan.morning: The Vijayanagara ruins across the boulder landscape, on a bicycle.
dayPlan.afternoon: Coracle crossings and the Tungabhadra river.
dayPlan.evening: Sunset from Matanga hill.
dayPlan.transport: Overnight train from Chennai or Bangalore

dayPlan.morning: Coffee estates in the Kodagu hills.
dayPlan.afternoon: Mysore's palace and market on the way down.
dayPlan.evening: Finish in Bangalore or return to Kochi.

title: European Summer Escape
subtitle: Lisbon, the Alps and the Amalfi Coast by rail and air
travelTime: Two short flights, the rest by train
overview: Sixteen days across three European climates — Atlantic city, alpine valley, Mediterranean coast — with enough time in each to stop moving. Built for June or September rather than August, and structured so that the two flights are the only stressful days.
packing: One warm layer and a rain shell for the Alps, even in July
Swimwear for both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean
Walking shoes that work on both alpine trails and cobbles
A rail app for Swiss and Italian bookings
A packing cube system — you will unpack three times

dayPlan.morning: Príncipe Real and the miradouros before the heat.
dayPlan.afternoon: Belém, or the train out to Cascais and the coast path.
dayPlan.evening: A small fado room in Alfama.

dayPlan.morning: Very early departure to be first through the gates at Pena.
dayPlan.afternoon: The Moorish castle walls and Quinta da Regaleira.
dayPlan.evening: Back to Lisbon; last dinner in Chiado.

dayPlan.morning: Fly to Zurich, then rail via Interlaken into the valley.
dayPlan.afternoon: Cable car up to car-free Mürren; the Eiger straight ahead.
dayPlan.evening: Half-board and an early night at 1,650m.

dayPlan.morning: Schilthorn ridge descent, or the Mürren–Gimmelwald path if the weather turns.
dayPlan.afternoon: Trümmelbach falls inside the mountain.
dayPlan.evening: Village silence after the last cable car.

dayPlan.morning: Fly to Naples; ferry along the coast to Praiano.
dayPlan.afternoon: Swim, then the terrace.
dayPlan.evening: Dinner facing the coastline.
dayPlan.transport: Flight plus ferry, half a day

dayPlan.morning: Ferry to Salerno or transfer to Naples.
dayPlan.afternoon: Fly home.
dayPlan.evening: Departure.
